common.runtimeOffline: This project's Runtime is offline. Run runharness again in the project terminal; the Web control plane cannot work without its TUI Runtime.

run.deleteDescription: Permanently delete this session, its runs, memory, evidence, isolated workspaces, and {{count}} image(s). Project files changed in-place are not deleted.
run.whatHappenedNote: Agent output and Runtime evidence are shown as recorded. Complete events remain in Process.
run.outcomeNote: Terminal state, iterations, and delivery mode.
run.nextObserve: Keep observing events and check output
run.nextPlanApproval: Review, revise, or approve the Plan to continue
run.nextPermissionApproval: Inspect the concrete action and choose an approval scope
run.nextInspect: Inspect failed checks and review issues
run.nextStopped: The run stopped; its existing process is still inspectable
run.nextDeliver: Inspect changes, then apply or discard them
run.nextDiscarded: The isolated result was discarded and did not change this project
run.nextComplete: Changes were written directly to this project
run.nextReviewPending: The review Agent did not complete a lifecycle decision. Retry from the TUI or override it after inspecting evidence.

approval.planHint: This is version {version}. Implementation will not start until approval; edit it directly to submit a revision.
approval.reasonPlaceholder: Explain a revision or rejection concretely
approval.permissionReasonPlaceholder: Optional: record why this action is allowed or rejected
approval.rejected: The user rejected the current Plan.
approval.saved: The decision was recorded and the Runtime is continuing.

process.title: Process timeline
process.note: Replay Agent, model, tool, and system events by round. Intermediate steps appear live.
process.emptyHint: Replayable evidence will appear here as the run progresses.

evaluation.checksNote: Real commands, durations, outcomes, and full output.
evaluation.reviewsNote: The reviewer, conclusion, and issues actually produced by the Runtime.
evaluation.noChecksHint: No fixed acceptance is configured. This is not a failure: Agents choose evidence from the task and repository, and their tool activity remains visible in Process.
evaluation.noReviewsHint: This run did not record an independent review.
evaluation.runningHint: The run has not reached this stage yet.
evaluation.reviewPendingHint: The Runtime retried the decision once, but the review Agent still did not successfully complete accept, request-changes, or unavailable. This is a review-service failure, not an in-place delivery or merge requirement. Retry with /continue in the TUI, or override it after inspecting the evidence below.
evaluation.serviceUnavailableTitle: The review Agent did not complete a lifecycle decision
evaluation.serviceFailurePlaceholder: Describe the evidence you inspected and why the current implementation is acceptable
evaluation.evidenceTitle: Inspect this implementation evidence before confirming
evaluation.noChangedFilesEvidence: No changed files were recorded, so the implementation cannot be confirmed.
evaluation.evidenceAcknowledgement: I inspected the changes, process, and validation evidence and understand this overrides the failed machine review.
evaluation.insufficientEvidence: There is not enough change evidence to confirm this implementation. Return to the TUI and use /continue to request more implementation or validation evidence.
evaluation.humanReason: Human review note (accepted issues enter the next Run; disputed findings stop blocking)
evaluation.reasonPlaceholder: If you disagree, explain the concrete reason
evaluation.alreadyReviewed: This review was already reviewed by a human.
evaluation.reviewUnavailable: This conclusion has no source verdict event, so it cannot receive a human review note.

result.title: Result and delivery
result.note: Inspect the changes and their workspace boundary.
result.inPlaceNote: These changes were written directly to the current project.
result.isolatedNote: This Session explicitly used an isolated workspace, so its changes are not in the live project yet. This is a delivery choice, not a Git conflict or a review required for every Run. The default in-place mode writes changes directly and needs no Apply step.
result.runningHint: Changes and delivery actions appear after the run ends.
result.missingHint: This terminal run has no readable development result.
result.continueHint: The Web UI is for observation and review. Return to the TUI, enter /session and choose this conversation, then submit new context; RunHarness creates a new Run without replaying completed steps.
result.noChangesHint: The run recorded no added, modified, or deleted files.
result.rawDiff: Structured view unavailable; show raw diff
result.binaryDiff: This binary file changed; no text diff is available.
result.noTextDiff: This file has no displayable text diff.

delivery.applied: The isolated result was applied to this project.
delivery.discarded: The isolated result was discarded and cannot be applied.
delivery.conflict: Delivery is blocked. Inspect the conflict evidence, reconcile the source or auxiliary worktree, then retry.

empty.title: Start the first run from your terminal
empty.body: The Web app observes, teaches, and manages the same project Runtime. Ordinary development starts in the TUI.
empty.step1: Run runharness in the project directory
empty.step2: Enter a development goal in the TUI
empty.step3: Return here to compare process, performance, review, and result

draft.unsavedHint: These changes are not active yet. Review them, then save once.
draft.savedHint: This page matches the saved configuration.

agents.title: Agent configuration
agents.note: Each Agent owns its command, model, arguments, and environment. Assign Agents to execution stages after configuring them.
agents.stagesNote: Planner and Generator use one primary Agent plus ordered fallbacks. Only Evaluator runs multiple reviewers in parallel.
agents.noFallback: No fallback. The run fails explicitly if the primary Agent is unavailable.
agents.reviewersHint: Selected reviewers run independently in parallel; conclusions are not averaged into a total score.
agents.invalidId: Agent IDs may only contain letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens.
agents.envInvalid: Environment must be valid JSON with string values.
agents.apiToolsHint: API Agents include a model → MCP tool → result loop. Their actions come from project MCP; without file or command tools they are best suited to planning, review, and remote-tool tasks.
agents.draftApplied: Field changes are in the page draft
agents.advanced: Advanced: edit the complete JSON configuration
agents.saved: Agent and stage configuration saved and reloaded.

tools.title: Project tools and MCP
tools.note: See which capabilities are Provider-owned or RunHarness-owned, where they execute, and which project MCP servers are connected.
tools.emptyHint: Add project tools only when they solve a real task; Agents keep their native capabilities.
tools.runtimesHint: RunHarness controls only actions dispatched through a listed controlled Runtime.
tools.providerCapabilitiesHint: These remain available to the Agent and are observed through Provider events; the Provider owns their execution boundary.
tools.acceptanceEmpty: No fixed acceptance is configured. Agents choose evidence from the task and repository.
tools.inheritsPolicyHint: Enabling a server only connects it; each tool call is decided by the project's built-in policy and optional Safety Agent.
tools.unknownDisabledTools: These disabled entries are not tools advertised by the server and have no effect: {tools}

runtime.title: Runtime policy
runtime.note: Edits stay in a draft until you save them for the next run.
runtime.iterationsHint: How many implementation and verification rounds may follow a failed review.
runtime.planReviewHint: Continue automatically by default, or require a human to review and revise the Plan.
runtime.workspaceHint: Controls where Agents may read or write, separately from action approval.
runtime.workspacePlacementHint: Choose whether Agents edit the live project or an isolated Session workspace.
runtime.workspaceAccessHint: Write access applies equally to Planner, Generator, and Evaluator.
runtime.materializeIgnoredHint: Optional project-relative paths, one per line. They are copied into isolated workspaces even when Git ignores them; caches and dependencies should stay omitted.
runtime.networkHint: Controls network access. Allow all does not override this boundary.
runtime.permissionModeHint: Controls approval for actions not matched by project rules; it never widens workspace or network boundaries.
runtime.safetyClassifierHint: Optional second-layer semantic control; it does not replace built-in policy.
runtime.safetyAgentHint: Choose one Agent/model to classify action risk.
runtime.classifierFallbackHint: How to continue after a timeout or invalid model output.

effectiveWorkspace.in_place_read_write: All Agent roles may write the current project; changes are live immediately.
effectiveWorkspace.in_place_read_only: All Agent roles may inspect the current project but cannot write it.
effectiveWorkspace.isolated_read_write: All Agent roles may write the Session workspace; Apply is required for delivery.
effectiveWorkspace.isolated_read_only: All Agent roles may inspect the isolated Session workspace but cannot write it.

effectiveNetwork.deny: Agent commands cannot access the network.
effectiveNetwork.allow_declared: Only provider- or project-declared network access is allowed.
effectiveNetwork.allow_all: Network access is allowed, still subject to provider and OS controls.

effectiveApproval.allow_all: RunHarness adds no prompt for unmatched actions; this does not bypass the sandbox.
effectiveApproval.dangerous_only: Destructive commands, credential paths, and external writes require approval.

runtime.effectiveRules: {count} project rules always run first; deny beats ask, and ask beats allow when several rules match.
runtime.catalogHint: These are the categories and examples recognized by the current RunHarness built-in policy.
runtime.catalogReadOnly: The built-in catalog is read-only. Add a project rule to change the outcome for a class of actions; rules cannot widen workspace or network boundaries or bypass the provider sandbox.

destructive_changes.title: Destructive, remote, and production changes
destructive_changes.description: Deletion, remote Git writes, infrastructure changes, publishing, and deployment require approval.

credential_access.title: Credentials, secrets, and sensitive paths
credential_access.description: Commands or paths that may expose credentials require approval.

external_network.title: External network origins
external_network.description: Managed network actions targeting a non-localhost origin require approval.

mcp_side_effects.title: MCP external side effects
mcp_side_effects.description: MCP-marked destructive, open-world write, or interactive browser actions require approval.

reversible_development.title: Normal reversible development
reversible_development.description: Project edits, checks, localhost browser validation, and read-only tools are allowed by default.

runtime.rulesLayerHint: Explicit allow, ask, or deny rules run first; the strictest matching result wins.
runtime.builtinLayerHint: The selected approval preset applies only when no project rule matches.
runtime.classifierOn: Enabled; it may preserve or tighten the first-layer result only.
runtime.classifierOff: Disabled; the first-layer policy remains fully active.
runtime.providerLayerHint: Claude, Codex, or Grok sandboxing and operating-system limits still apply.
runtime.rulesHint: Project rules match before the built-in policy. A match directly selects allow, ask, or deny; the strictest result wins when several rules match. RunHarness hard-blocks API/MCP actions it directly mediates; commands inside a CLI Agent also depend on that provider's native sandbox and rules.
runtime.noRules: No project rules yet; every action relies on the approval preset and built-in decision catalog above.

prompts.title: Prompt slots
prompts.note: System instructions and user context are editable and versioned; Runtime permission boundaries are not controlled by prompts.
prompts.activationHint: This mapping comes from the shared Prompt contract and matches real Runtime calls, not page-defined stages.
prompts.snapshotNote: Each Run records prompt_snapshot versions. Saving affects later compose calls only and never rewrites evidence from an earlier Run.
prompts.safetyNote: The Safety Agent runs only after the deterministic built-in policy allows an action and may preserve or tighten that result. Prompts cannot bypass Runtime, Provider, or operating-system boundaries.
prompts.unsaved: Unsaved changes; saving creates a new version

slots.common_kernel: Shared evidence, workspace, recovery, and role boundaries for Planner, Generator, and Evaluator.
slots.planner_kernel: System instructions used while Planner defines objectives, non-goals, risks, and acceptance.
slots.generator_kernel: System instructions used while Generator implements, verifies, and records deviations from the plan.
slots.evaluator_kernel: System instructions used while Evaluator independently checks the repository and evidence and emits a Review control signal.
slots.safety_classifier_kernel: Used by the optional Safety Agent to classify an action already allowed by the built-in policy.
slots.product_intent: Product goal, intended user, and shortest path through the core task.
slots.acceptance_preferences: Preferred validation evidence, deterministic checks, and quality judgment.
slots.trust_boundary: Boundary between the trusted workspace and external services, credentials, production systems, and human authorization.
slots.project_conventions: Repository instructions, architecture, naming, tests, and package-manager conventions.
slots.reference_examples: Relevant positive or negative examples for planning and acceptance only; it is not injected into implementation.

planner_plan.title: Planner produces the plan
planner_plan.detail: Injected after a Run is created or continued and before plan_proposed. Planner inspects the repository and forms the plan without implementing it.

generator_iteration.title: Generator implements each iteration
generator_iteration.detail: Injected on every Generator call after plan approval. Feedback iterations continue using the snapshot fixed for that Run.

evaluator_review.title: Evaluator performs independent review
evaluator_review.detail: Injected after Generator finishes and Runtime collects checks and changes. Evaluator then calls a Review control tool to decide the lifecycle outcome.

safety_classification.title: Optional secondary Safety classification
safety_classification.detail: Injected only when built-in policy returned allow and an enabled Safety Agent is configured. Classification cannot widen an existing boundary.

learn.fromArticles: From four reference articles to a real implementation
learn.seeIt: See evidence in the current run

harness-design.title: Harness design
harness-design.lead: A Harness is not one model call. It organizes goals, implementation, verification, and feedback into an observable loop.
harness-design.implementationMapHint: Follow the development loop into Session event storage, then see how acceptance evidence closes the implementation and feedback loop.

1.title: A goal enters a Session
1.body: The Session keeps the conversation while each Run reaches a terminal state and its event log preserves the evidence.

2.title: Planner defines the path
2.body: Planner focuses on intent, boundaries, and acceptance without doing Generator's implementation work.

3.title: Generator uses tools
3.body: Implementation actions stay inside the workspace and record tool calls and results.

4.title: Evidence and Evaluator close the loop
4.body: Configured deterministic checks and Agent-selected tools provide evidence; independent review completes the run or returns feedback without imposing a fixed tool sequence.

harness-design.evidence: Inspect structured handoffs from Planner and Generator
harness-design.manage: Adjust user goals, completion criteria, and preferences in Prompt slots.

auto-mode.title: Auto Mode and safety boundaries
auto-mode.lead: Automation comes from actions that can be classified, denied, and stopped—not unlimited permission.
auto-mode.implementationMapHint: Trace permission decisions, controlled tool signals, and failure terminal states to see how automatic execution remains deniable and stoppable.

1.title: Classify each action
1.body: Read-only checks, project writes, and high-risk actions use distinct boundaries.

2.title: Probe tool output
2.body: Output is checked before it enters model context.

3.title: Record denial reasons
3.body: A denial is a structured event, so the user can see what happened.

4.title: Terminal states end loops
4.body: Cancellation, permission denial, iteration limits, and execution failures produce explicit terminal state and recovery evidence.

auto-mode.evidence: Inspect safety denial and stop events
auto-mode.manage: Choose the built-in permission policy, Plan approval, and whether to enable the optional Safety Agent classifier in Runtime settings.

managed-agents.title: Managed Agents
managed-agents.lead: An Agent is an executor jointly managed by its Session, role, context, and workspace.
managed-agents.implementationMapHint: Read from Agent routing and the backend contract through workspace management to understand the boundary between brain and hands.

1.title: Session lives outside context
1.body: A model window can reset while append-only events preserve real state.

2.title: Brain and hands are separate
2.body: Models make judgments; tools perform bounded actions through stable interfaces.

3.title: Structured handoffs
3.body: A handoff gives the next role clear input and gives the user a replayable boundary.

4.title: Recovery and workspace boundaries
4.body: In-place edits are live; isolated Sessions retain one primary worktree, allow observable auxiliary worktrees, and require explicit conflict-checked delivery.

managed-agents.evidence: Inspect Agent completion, handoff, and recovery evidence
managed-agents.manage: Configure primary and fallback Agents for Planner/Generator, and multiple independent reviewers for Evaluator.

long-running.title: Long-running work and recovery
long-running.lead: Long tasks stay manageable when progress is durable, work is incremental, context can be rebuilt, and every Run reaches an explicit state.
long-running.implementationMapHint: Trace durable Session events, recovery Memory, and bounded Run context to see how long tasks continue across model windows.

1.title: Persist progress outside the model
1.body: Events, results, Memory, Context, and progress files survive a model window or Runtime restart.

2.title: Work in bounded Runs
2.body: Each user submission is incremental work with an explicit completed, failed, stopped, or durable waiting state.

3.title: Rebuild only relevant context
3.body: Budgeted Memory and referenced files carry decisions, failures, and evidence forward without replaying every token.

4.title: Resume without inventing history
4.body: Continue, Steer, approvals, and provider-session recovery reuse persisted facts and the real workspace state.

long-running.evidence: Inspect terminal states, progress, Memory, and recovery events
long-running.manage: Manage iteration limits, Plan approval, and durable Runtime policy.
